newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks down sharply on Beximco speculation.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks down sharply on Beximco speculation.

text.p: Dhaka stocks ended sharply down on market speculation about the future of Beximco group, Bangladesh's largest corporate house, brokers said.
The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) all-share price index dropped 45.31 points or 4.5 percent to 960.26 on turnover of 46.2 million taka. Losers led gainers by 116 to 20.
Singer Bangladesh lost 315 taka to 4,969, Beximco Denims dropped 16 to 166 and Apex Foods declined 159 to 1,647.
Broker Imtyiaz Hosain said: "Worries over the fate of the country's largest corporate group triggered selling in the market."

Beximco has accused the central bank of leaking malicious information to the press following a reported move by Bangladesh Bank (central bank) Governor Lutfar Rahman sarkar to stop fresh bank lending to Beximco.
The central bank says the group has defaulted on previous loans, but Beximco has said it is being discriminated against by the bank.
Brokers were concerned that some of the Beximco companies might be closed for want of working capital.

They said market sentiment was depressed also because of a planned country-wide 24-hour strike on Wednesday by Bangladesh's top labour union. The bourse is expected to remain closed on Wednesday if the strike shuts communications.
